version: SAGI VIEWPOINT V2.6 · TACTICAL FRAME GUARD

lesson_markers.label: Lateral shift weakness and space behind
Same numbers, different players; people make the system

chapters.purpose: hook the lesson without explaining ahead of the formation
show the complete 4-3-2-1 structure before any tactical movement
explain how central control becomes width, between-lines access and final-third execution

rules: pure black negative space
pitch only slightly brighter than background
thin neutral-grey field lines
flat clean yellow own-team silhouettes
muted neutral-grey opponents
no visible specular sheen
no decorative lighting
no heavy cast shadows
visual hierarchy must read tactics before materials
clean_core.rule_added: Preserve near-black pitch values without AgX lifting dark tones.
clean_core.root_fix: Convert authored HEX sRGB palette values to Blender linear material values before rendering.
clean_core.expected_result: near-black pitch remains near-black on output while yellow/grey preserve intended display colors

camera_rail.principle: follow attack/defence mainly along pitch length; side actions stay inside a wider frame instead of pulling the camera laterally

camera_continuity.principle: Hold the current view unless a tactical question requires a new viewpoint; small screen-axis changes settle quickly.

central_master.principle: use a lower oblique floating-pitch master so the near end reads larger and the far end compresses, matching Teactics spatial depth while retaining the whole board
rules: pitch board centre owns composition in CENTRAL_MASTER
show the full physical board silhouette, not only the white touchlines
preserve dark breathing room around the board so it reads as suspended in space
do not let player clusters drag the master shot off-centre
use the floating master briefly as spatial orientation, then return to tactical relation framing

visual_integrity.rule: Every tactical shot must preserve both the local relation and enough formation structure to understand where it belongs.
visual_integrity.minimum_context: carrier + next option + nearest defender + two structural anchors
visual_integrity.edge_safe_rule: No tactical subject should sit on or be clipped by the portrait-frame edge.
visual_integrity.background_rule: Wide tactical views may reveal more board, but must never reveal a hard visual void beyond the pitch.
visual_integrity.field_scope_rule: The amount of pitch visible must be chosen by tactical information need, not by a fixed camera aesthetic.

full_lesson_director.principle: TACTICS FIRST. Camera language exists only to reveal tactical cause, relation, space and consequence.
global_rules: show the whole structure before explaining a local relationship
camera changes only when the tactical question changes
local shots must retain enough anchors to understand where the action belongs
ball movement owns transition timing during attacking execution
camera follows attack/defense mainly longitudinally; lateral action is contained by wider framing
do not search for the next receiver before the pass makes that receiver tactically relevant
use CENTRAL_MASTER as chapter reset, not as decoration
defensive switches are explained by widening the tactical picture before moving local
no dramatic climax treatment; completeness and causality come first

formation: How are the three midfielders layered?
Where do the two attacking midfielders live?
What is the lone striker's reference point?
attack: How are the spaces between lines occupied?
How does strong-side attraction create the final action?
defense: How is the ball forced wide?
How does the fullback-midfielder-center-back triangle protect the flank?
Why is repeated lateral switching the weakness?
How does the block recover central compactness?
summary: What does the system give you?
Why do player qualities determine whether the shape works?

full_lesson_director.possession_reset_rule: chapter_state.ball_owner explicitly resets the tactical ball owner at chapter boundaries
full_lesson_director.summary_possession_note: Summary circulation explicitly returns from Seedorf to Pirlo before the flank-risk example, preserving continuous possession logic.

locked_rules: pitch stays visually central with black breathing room around it
players read smaller than TEST14 local close-ups but remain identifiable
top title and subtitle must not overlap the tactical pitch body
full horizontal width is mandatory whenever fullbacks, flank overloads or switches are explained
camera follows the phase longitudinally; it does not chase the ball laterally
attack actions and timing remain unchanged

camera_scale_notes.build: semi-global structure, not a close Pirlo portrait
camera_scale_notes.between_lines: structural crop allowed, but both half-spaces remain readable
camera_scale_notes.strong_side_overlap: keep opposite side in frame; no right-channel crop
camera_scale_notes.final_third: retain attacking two-thirds instead of final-third-only crop
camera_scale_notes.finish: slightly tighter structure while keeping goal + surrounding defenders
camera_scale_notes.exit: return to full-pitch floating view before defense chapter

viewpoint_language.principle: Tactical question chooses viewing direction. Shot scale chooses size. Field scope protects required context.

HIGH_ANGLE_MASTER.purpose: formation, width, both flanks, spatial reset

THREE_QUARTER_OBLIQUE.purpose: main structural relation with readable depth

TOP_DOWN_TACTICAL.purpose: shape, zones, compactness and horizontal distances

LOW_ANGLE_LONGITUDINAL.purpose: between-lines depth, behind/in-front relationships, vertical lanes

RIGHT_FLANK_DIAGONAL.purpose: right-flank overlap and half-space channel while retaining central reference

LEFT_FLANK_DIAGONAL.purpose: left-flank overlap and half-space channel while retaining central reference

LOW_ANGLE_LATERAL.purpose: horizontal line spacing and side-on pressing relationships

GOAL_FACING_AXIAL.purpose: final pass, striker movement, centre-backs, goalkeeper and goal in one depth picture

transition_rules: do not change viewpoint unless the tactical question changes
show width from high before entering a flank diagonal
show between-lines with longitudinal depth rather than top-down scale alone
return to high master after the finishing action
viewpoint transition may orbit, but tactical target must remain spatially continuous

canonical_terms.HIGH_ANGLE_MASTER: High-angle master view for whole-team structure, width and spatial reset.
canonical_terms.THREE_QUARTER_OBLIQUE: Three-quarter oblique view for readable depth while preserving team structure.
canonical_terms.TOP_DOWN_TACTICAL: Top-down tactical view for shape, zones, spacing and compactness.
canonical_terms.LOW_ANGLE_LONGITUDINAL: Low-angle longitudinal view along the pitch axis for vertical depth and between-the-lines relationships.
canonical_terms.RIGHT_FLANK_DIAGONAL: Right-flank diagonal view for overlaps, wide combinations and half-space access while retaining central reference.
canonical_terms.LEFT_FLANK_DIAGONAL: Left-flank diagonal view for overlaps, wide combinations and half-space access while retaining central reference.
canonical_terms.LOW_ANGLE_LATERAL: Low-angle lateral view across the pitch for horizontal line spacing and side-on pressing relationships.
canonical_terms.GOAL_FACING_AXIAL: Goal-facing axial view for final-pass depth, striker movement, centre-backs, goalkeeper and goal.

field_scope_terms.FLOATING_BOARD: Full floating tactical board silhouette retained.

composition_standard.benchmark: TEACTICS 71s reference video supplied by user
composition_standard.principle: The pitch is a floating tactical stage inside the 9:16 canvas. Screen placement adapts to the viewpoint; it is not defined by a fixed top or bottom percentage.
rules: Do not let the near edge of the tactical stage sit on the bottom frame edge as a default composition.
Re-center the tactical stage in screen space whenever viewpoint angle changes.
Preserve dark negative space below the active tactical stage when the reference viewpoint calls for it.
Title space, pitch space and lower breathing space must read as separate visual zones.
Do not create layout space by changing the tactical target or hiding required field context.
Full-width phases must preserve the touchlines; depth phases must preserve the near/far reference needed to understand vertical relationships.
A close tactical relation may crop non-essential board edges, but never crop the tactical landmark currently being explained.
composition_standard.acceptance: Judge against the Teactics reference frame-by-frame, not against a fixed percentage.

evaluate: does each angle answer the tactical question better than scale-only framing
is full width visible before and during flank explanation
does right overlap preserve touchline plus central reference
does finish show striker-centrebacks-goalkeeper-goal as one depth relation
viewpoint_test_notes.language_rule: All internal camera-direction, framing and field-scope terminology is authored in standardized English. Chinese is reserved for viewer-facing titles, subtitles and voice-over.
teactics_composition_acceptance: compare each viewpoint against the supplied Teactics reference, not a fixed safe-area percentage
near pitch edge must not default to touching the bottom frame edge
pitch should read as a floating tactical stage with dark breathing space around it
top title zone and lower breathing zone must remain visually independent from the tactical stage
viewpoint changes may alter the amount of bottom space; tactical clarity decides the composition

player_visual.principle: Smaller floating pitch, but players remain clearly upright and human-readable.

camera_path_smoothing.principle: Teactics-like camera discipline: hold the view when it still explains the concept; transition directly and briefly only when necessary.

readability_standard.locked_baseline: V1.3 viewpoint grammar and adaptive composition
changes: players +16-18% base readability, primary players +8% emphasis
flank diagonals reduced to 23 degrees to preserve orientation
tactical arrows, pass links and channel highlights added only when they explain the current tactical question
pitch landmarks and spatial bands raised slightly while remaining low-contrast
camera viewpoint changes use an orbital midpoint path
defensive reactions expand from isolated shifts to unit-level responses
exclusions: no decorative graphics unrelated to tactical explanation

v14_acceptance: Players are immediately readable in wide views without enlarging the pitch.
Right-flank diagonal remains recognisably aligned with the pitch.
Every tactical graphic explains a current decision, route or space; no decorative overlays.
Pitch landmarks remain visible in dark scenes without becoming visually dominant.
Camera transitions feel like one camera moving around one tactical board.
Defensive units react together so the viewer can see why space opens.

scale_script.v15_principle: Use camera scale, not player-model inflation, to make the active tactical relation dominant.

tactical_emphasis_standard.principle: Every phase tells the viewer where to look: master context -> focused relation -> readable hold -> next relation.

hierarchy.CONTEXT: All other players remain visible without editorial ring.

tactical_graphics_v15.principle: Graphics explain the tactical question and disappear when the question changes.
tactical_graphics_v15.zone_style: low-contrast filled tactical surface; not a UI card
tactical_graphics_v15.path_style: restrained dashed or gently curved movement route

tactical_hold_standard.principle: Relationship forms, camera settles, viewer reads, then the next movement begins.

v15_acceptance: Wide structure remains wide; only the active tactical relation receives a meaningful scale change.
At every key phase the viewer can identify FOCAL, SUPPORT and CONTEXT without text.
Movement routes read as dashed/curved tactical language and spaces read as filled zones, not UI rectangles.
Key relations receive 0.55-0.80 seconds of camera stability before the next camera transition.
No title, subtitle or logo is rendered.

emphasis_visual.principle: At the smaller stable pitch scale, rings remain legible but secondary to the tactical relation.

v16_balance_standard.benchmark: Exact Teactics 71s reference supplied by user
v16_balance_standard.principle: Preserve emphasis capability while restoring tactical coordinates and context.
rules: FOCUS_RELATION must retain at least one tactical landmark whenever possible.
Focused shots should retain 3-5 relationship players, not isolate one actor.
Use camera height and distance before adding orbit rotation.
Filled zones remain subordinate to players and movement paths.
TACTICAL_HOLD stabilizes the camera; it does not freeze tactical life.
No title, subtitle or logo.

v16_acceptance: No key focus shot reads as a player close-up detached from the pitch.
Pitch direction remains obvious through the right-flank and final-third phases.
Focal player is found first, but support/context players remain readable.
Filled tactical zones never become the dominant visual object.
Dashed routes appear close to the related action and clear quickly.
Tactical holds preserve readable relationships without dead-frame feeling.

v17_standard.benchmark: Exact 71s Teactics reference supplied by user
v17_standard.principle: One shot, one tactical question. Emphasis never sacrifices tactical coordinates.
rules: Exactly 11 opponent players exist in the scene.
Focused relations retain 3-5 relevant players plus one authored tactical landmark.
Player readability comes from a slimmer silhouette and clearer facing direction, not larger overall scale.
Only one tactical graphic class may accompany emphasis in each tactical phase.
Camera uses height and distance before orbit rotation.
No title, subtitle or logo.

v17_acceptance: No focused shot loses all pitch landmarks.
Players read as miniature footballers rather than blocky chess pieces.
No phase carries competing zone, route and pass-link graphics at the same time.
The tactical relation remains more important than the visual effect.

director_constraints.principle: Default to axial viewing; use only tiny lateral observation changes when needed.

floating_stage.principle: Match Teactics floating-board scale: generous dark space around the tactical stage, with modest concept-driven scale changes.

graphic_semantics.rule: One shot answers one tactical question. Multiple graphic types are allowed only when they explain the same question.

concepts.ATTACK_MIDFIELD_WIDTH: How do the midfielders create passing angles?
concepts.ATTACK_BETWEEN_LINES: Where is the receiving space between lines?
concepts.ATTACK_FULLBACK_WIDTH: How is width created without wingers?
concepts.ATTACK_STRONG_SIDE_OVERLAP: How does the outside runner create the overload?
concepts.ATTACK_FINAL_THIRD_FLOW: How does Kaka attack the final gap?
concepts.ATTACK_FINISH_RELATION: How does Inzaghi exploit the broken line?

v18_standard.benchmark: Exact 71s Teactics reference supplied by user
v18_standard.principle: Camera follows tactical concepts, not the ball.
rules: Do not add a camera change inside the same tactical concept unless spatial understanding would otherwise fail.
Structural axis rotation is capped at 8 degrees; relation shots at 15 degrees; finish at 12 degrees.
The floating pitch remains vertically stable inside the 9:16 canvas.
Players remain readable as upright human symbols from wide tactical shots.
A shot may combine several graphics only when every graphic explains the same tactical question.
No title, subtitle or logo.

v18_acceptance: No redundant push-in occurs during the Pirlo build or between-lines concept.
The pitch longitudinal axis never appears to spin between structural phases.
The board keeps a stable floating-stage position through viewpoint changes.
Players remain identifiable as people without relying on a tighter camera.
Fullback-width phase may use zones, emphasis and routes together because they communicate one concept.
Every camera transition can be justified by a change in tactical question.

teactics_similarity_target.basis: Exact 71s Teactics reference supplied by user
teactics_similarity_target.v25_focus: Fix V2.4 hidden distance clamp, reduce pitch-to-canvas size 8-10%, and restore Teactics-like controlled 0 to ±4° viewpoint variety without losing stability.
teactics_similarity_target.pass_rule: Do not claim 90%+ until rendered V2.5 is reopened and compared frame-by-frame against the exact reference.

v19_acceptance: No camera change occurs at midfield-width if the previous structural view still explains it.
No separate camera change occurs for final-third flow if the overlap view still explains it.
Structural pitch axis stays visually stable with zero authored azimuth.
Focused flank view stays within 8 degrees of longitudinal alignment.
Floating board scale stays inside the authored z envelope for each shot scale.
Players remain readable without extra camera push-in.
Every surviving camera transition is justified by a tactical explanation need.
v20_acceptance: Structural pitch occupies a clearly smaller share of the 9:16 frame than V1.9.
Players are visibly larger relative to the pitch without tighter camera framing.
No authored tactical shot exceeds 4 degrees azimuth.
No right-side or finishing phase reads as a spinning pitch.
Miniature players remain upright and readable while limb motion stays restrained.
Graphics remain readable at the smaller pitch scale.
Exact-reference comparison must score at least 90/100 before this stage is accepted.
v21_acceptance: Pitch longitudinal axis remains visually stable in all tactical shots.
No right-side or finishing shot makes the board appear to roll in screen space.
Floating board leaves more dark negative space than V2.0.
Players remain clearly readable despite the smaller pitch.
Reference comparison must score at least 90/100 before acceptance.

screen_axis_lock.principle: Allow only small authored screen-axis changes tied to tactical questions; never decorative roll.

screen_scale_lock.principle: Keep a smaller Teactics-like floating board with stable apparent size across focal lengths.

v22_acceptance: Apparent floating-pitch size stays stable across structural, flank and finishing phases.
No finishing shot suddenly fills the 9:16 frame.
Pitch longitudinal axis remains stable in screen space.
Perspective depth is more Teactics-like than V2.1 without board roll.
Miniature players remain clearly human-readable at the smaller pitch scale.
Reference score must reach at least 90/100 before acceptance.
v23_acceptance: Compare 12-43 seconds against exact Teactics reference
Keep pitch visible and stable with no focal breathing
Restore legible pitch line contrast and human player silhouette
v24_acceptance: Maintain native 30fps and V2.3 floating-stage stability.
Pitch perspective has stronger near/far depth without screen-axis roll.
Players read as upright miniature humans rather than dots or flat markers.
No tactical phase uses decorative camera movement.
Exact-reference score must reach at least 90/100 before acceptance.
v25_acceptance: Floating pitch is visibly smaller than V2.4 while players stay readable.
Camera viewpoints differ subtly by tactical question instead of remaining mechanically identical.
No decorative camera roll or unnecessary camera change.
Exact-reference score must reach at least 90/100 before acceptance.

frame_guard.principle: Preserve the whole tactical board during late-phase camera retargeting; avoid clipped goal and lower board edge.

v26_acceptance: no cropped active pitch landmark during 12–43s
compare exact Teactics reference before claiming 90
